task_3.title: Revert early teardown on session stop/fail
task_3.description: Pytest 8.0.2 reverts the 8.0.0 change that forced immediate teardown when a session was stopping or failing. The rollback avoids a regression where distributed runs using `--maxfail` could execute session-scoped fixture teardown more than once after the failure limit was reached.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that stopping a test session after reaching `--maxfail` does not cause session-scoped fixture teardown to run more than once in distributed pytest runs, while preserving normal teardown behavior when the session stops or fails.

expectation.grounded: When pytest 8.0.2 runs test items through `runtestprotocol`, reaching a session `shouldfail` or `shouldstop` state must no longer force teardown as though there is no next item. In particular, runs using `--maxfail` with pytest-xdist must not trigger duplicate teardown execution for session-scoped fixtures after the failure limit is reached.
expectation.conceptual: If a test run stops because the failure limit or another stop condition is reached, fixture cleanup should still occur exactly once. Distributed execution should not duplicate session-level teardown just because the run terminated early.

constraints.grounded: Do not preserve the reverted eager-teardown behavior tied to session `shouldfail` or `shouldstop`. Teardown must continue through the normal item teardown flow and must not introduce duplicate session fixture finalization in pytest-xdist when `--maxfail` is reached.
constraints.conceptual: Early termination must remain safe: cleanup should happen reliably, but the framework must not over-clean up or finalize shared fixtures multiple times because a stop condition was hit.

behavior: Pytest no longer switches teardown into an immediate end-of-session path solely because the session is marked to fail or stop.
When `--maxfail` stops execution in a distributed run, session-scoped fixture teardown is not performed twice for the worker that hit the failure limit.
Teardown continues to follow normal sequencing relative to the next collected item instead of being forced into a terminal teardown state on session stop/fail.
acceptance_criteria: When a pytest-xdist run reaches its `--maxfail` threshold in one worker, session-scoped fixture teardown for that worker should execute only once.

When a test session enters a stop or fail state during item execution, pytest should still emit normal teardown behavior without forcing all remaining fixture cleanup to behave as though there is no next item.
When execution stops early, users should observe cleanup occurring without duplicate session-level finalization side effects.

task_1.title: Restore Windows short-path collection matching
task_1.description: Pytest 8.0.2 fixes a Windows collection regression introduced in 8.0.1 where invoking pytest with a short 8.3-style path could cause valid tests to be skipped because the requested path and the collected path were compared as different strings even though they pointed to the same filesystem location.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest on Windows still collects the intended tests when the user starts collection with a short 8.3 path that refers to the same file or directory as the corresponding long path seen during collection.

expectation.grounded: On Windows, when `pytest` or `python -m pytest` is invoked with an explicit file or directory path in short 8.3 form, collection should treat that path as matching the corresponding long-form collected `Path` target if both refer to the same filesystem entry. A path representation mismatch between short and long Windows forms must not cause the requested target to be excluded from collection.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to run pytest against a Windows path regardless of whether it is written in short or long form. If both spellings identify the same location, pytest should collect and run the tests there normally.

constraints.grounded: The behavior change should be limited to Windows path matching for explicitly requested collection targets when direct path equality would otherwise fail only because one path is short-form and the other is long-form. Existing behavior for non-Windows platforms, already-equal paths, and genuinely different filesystem targets should remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should address the Windows short-path regression without broadening collection to unrelated paths or changing collection semantics on other platforms.

behavior: Pytest should recognize short 8.3 Windows paths and long Windows paths as the same collection target when they resolve to the same filesystem location.
Invoking pytest with a short-form directory path on Windows should still collect tests discovered under the matching long-form directory.
A collection mismatch caused only by short-versus-long Windows path representation should no longer result in valid tests being omitted or a zero-tests-collected outcome for that target.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Windows directory containing discoverable tests, when pytest is invoked with that directory using its short 8.3 path, then the tests in that directory should be collected and run.

Given a Windows test file selected through a short 8.3 path, when the same file is discovered under its long path form during collection, then pytest should treat both as the same target and include the file in collection.
When a supplied path and a collected path refer to different filesystem entries, pytest should not treat them as the same target solely because their textual representations differ.

task_2.title: Prevent internal IndexError during source statement analysis
task_2.description: Pytest 8.0.2 fixes an internal crash in source statement analysis. When pytest evaluates source ranges for a statement and the relevant slice begins on a blank line, it should continue normal processing instead of failing with an internal IndexError.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 8.0.2 prevents pytest from crashing with an internal IndexError while determining source statement ranges, including edge cases where the analyzed source segment begins with a blank line.

expectation.grounded: When pytest computes statement ranges through getstatementrange_ast, an empty starting source line must be treated as a valid input state. If the first analyzed line is blank, block and statement detection should continue without raising an internal IndexError, while preserving the existing handling of indented and non-indented non-empty starting lines.
expectation.conceptual: Pytest should robustly analyze source statements even when the relevant code segment starts with an empty line. Users should no longer see an internal framework crash in this scenario; pytest should continue normal processing and only surface real application or test outcomes.

constraints.grounded: Do not alter normal statement-range behavior for non-empty starting lines. Indentation-sensitive block detection must remain unchanged for indented lines, top-level handling must remain unchanged for non-indented lines, and the fix must only remove the empty-line IndexError edge case without introducing new warnings or exceptions.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should be narrowly scoped to eliminating the crash on blank-line inputs. Existing behavior for ordinary source layouts must stay stable, with no new regressions in how pytest identifies statement boundaries.

behavior: If source statement analysis begins on an empty line, pytest no longer raises an internal IndexError.
If the starting source line is non-empty and begins with whitespace, pytest continues to treat it as an already-started indented block for statement-range detection.
If the starting source line is non-empty and does not begin with whitespace, pytest continues normal top-level statement detection unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest analyzes a source segment whose first relevant line is blank, it should not fail with an internal IndexError.
When pytest analyzes a source segment whose first relevant line is indented, it should continue normal block-oriented statement detection.
When pytest analyzes a source segment whose first relevant line is non-empty and not indented, it should preserve existing statement detection behavior apart from the crash fix.
